title: Conflict-Free Coloring Planar Graphs with 4 Colors
summary: We efficiently conflict-free color every planar graph with 4 colors. An (open-neighborhood) conflict-free coloring assigns colors to vertices in a way that every vertex v has a neighbor w such that the color of w is distinct from the colors of the other neighbors of v (i.e., the color of w is unique in the open neighborhood of v). A previous best upper bound on the conflict-free chromatic number of planar graphs was 5, and it is known that 4 colors are sometimes necessary.
